question.text: Will the French government invoke Article 49.3 on the 2027 finance bill (PLF 2027) before December 18, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as **Yes** if, before December 18, 2026 Central European Standard Time, the prime minister of France officially invokes Article 49.3 to attempt to pass the 2027 [budget](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/dossiers/PLF_2027) without an ordinary vote in the National Assembly. This counts whether this is used for the entire bill or just a section of it, regardless of the round of the Assembly's consideration.
question.fine_print: Only an actual engagement of responsibility in the Assemblée nationale chamber counts; a Council of Ministers authorization to use 49.3, public statements of intent, or the adoption of the budget by ordinances (Article 47) do not count. A 49.3 invocation on the 2027 social security financing bill (PLFSS 2027) or any other text does not count. An invocation on the PLF 2027 that occurred before this question opened does not count, but a further invocation within the window does.

# PLF 2027 and Article 49.3: research brief (as of 2026-11-09)

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-11-09: The Assemblée nationale's PLF 2027 dossier (bill n° 3210) records these steps: filed 1 October 2026, plenary debate from 13 October, and the bill **rejected** at first reading on 4 November 2026 (T.A. n° 362). It shows **no 49.3 engagement**, and no Senate or joint committee (CMP) stage is listed yet. [AN dossier](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/dossiers/PLF_2027)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. No 49.3 has been used on the PLF 2027. Because the Assembly rejected the revenue part, the bill went to the Senate in the government's original version, and the Assembly never debated the spending part. A 49.3 is now only possible at the Assembly's **nouvelle lecture** (second reading) or lecture définitive (final reading), both after the Senate vote and a failed CMP.
- The timing is tight. The Senate votes on 9 December, a CMP is targeted for "mid-December" with no date set, and a nouvelle lecture in the Assembly would have to start and reach a 49.3 by 17 December. [Public Sénat](https://www.publicsenat.fr/actualites/politique/budget-2027-calendrier-49-3-ordonnancesquelles-sont-les-echeances-a-venir-et-les-scenarios-possibles)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-09: L'Express says Lecornu faces a "cornelian choice" between 49.3 and budget ordinances after the "historic" 458-0 rejection. I could not open this page to verify it; the summary comes from the news API. [L'Express](https://www.lexpress.fr/economie/budget-493-ou-ordonnances-le-choix-cornelien-de-sebastien-lecornu-QHKOU5BOK5DJ5EEISC3QOT6COY/)
- 2026-11-09: The Senate starts examining the budgets. It debates the PLFSS (social security budget) until 18 November and the PLF from 20 November to 9 December. Economy Minister Lescure calls the economy "stalled" after GDP shrank in Q3. [Sud Ouest](https://www.sudouest.fr/economie/finances/budget-de-l-etat-et-de-la-secu-2027-balayes-par-l-assemblee-les-textes-arrivent-des-ce-lundi-au-senat-dans-un-climat-d-incertitude-31452987.php), [La Libre](https://www.lalibre.be/dernieres-depeches/2026/11/09/budget-le-senat-prend-la-main-lincertitude-demeure-ICEVDWMDFFG25OC5CM5F5AE7NI/)
- 2026-11-06: There are two ways to count the 70-day point after which ordinances are allowed. Counting from the 9 October start of the clock gives 17 December. Counting from the 1 October filing gives 10 December. The site also reports that Lecornu ruled out both 49.3 and ordinances on 17 September 2026, attributing this to Public Sénat; I could not find the original statement. [Courrier des Stratèges](https://lecourrierdesstrateges.fr/budget-2027-apres-le-rejet-que-va-t-il-se-passer-maintenant)
- 2026-11-05: Lecornu's office says the "time for compromise" will come after the Senate's review in December. Budget Minister Amiel says only a few weeks remain. [Euronews](https://fr.euronews.com/2026/11/05/budget-2027-lassemblee-nationale-rejette-le-texte-a-lunanimite)
- 2026-11-04: The Assembly rejects the revenue part 458-0 with 2 abstentions. Government-camp groups also voted against (EPR 63, Horizons 35, Dem 27). [Zinfos974](https://www.zinfos974.com/les-deputes-rejettent-unanimement-le-projet-de-loi-de-finances-2027-au-tour-des-senateurs-de-voter/)
- 2026-11-03: Public Sénat says the government was not expected to use 49.3 at first reading, despite calls from Yaël Braun-Pivet. Other key dates: 11 December is the deadline to request a separate vote on spending, 17 December the 70-day point, and 19 December the deadline to file a special finance law. [Public Sénat](https://www.publicsenat.fr/actualites/politique/budget-2027-calendrier-49-3-ordonnancesquelles-sont-les-echeances-a-venir-et-les-scenarios-possibles)
- 2026-08-22: In a letter, Lecornu refused to decide in advance between 49.3 and ordinances, saying it was not "raisonnable, ni souhaitable" (reasonable or desirable) to do so. [21News](https://www.21news.be/budget-2027-lecornu-refuse-de-parler-deja-de-49-3-et-appelle-au-compromis/)
- Undated (before 30 September): PS leader Olivier Faure threatened censure if the budget resembles the Attal or Philippe programmes. [TRT Français](https://www.trtfrancais.com/article/24c036a1f892)

## 4. Base rates (was 49.3 used on the PLF before 18 December?)
- PLF 2023, autumn 2022: **Yes**. Borne first used it on 19 October 2022, then several more times.
- PLF 2024, autumn 2023: **Yes**. Borne used it from 18 October 2023.
- PLF 2025, autumn 2024: **No**. Barnier fell on 4 December 2024 after a 49.3 on the PLFSS, which does not count here. Bayrou then used 49.3 on the PLF in late January and February 2025.
- PLF 2026, autumn 2025: **No**. Lecornu gave up 49.3 in October 2025, the CMP failed around 19 December, and a special law was passed. He then used 49.3 three times between 20 and 30 January 2026. [LCP](https://lcp.fr/actualites/budget-2026-sebastien-lecornu-enclenche-un-ultime-493-ouvrant-la-voie-a-l-adoption), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/2/france-adopts-2026-budget-after-two-no-confidence-votes-fail)
- Overall: 2 of the last 4 years, and 0 of the 2 years since the government lost its working majority in 2024. In 2025, as now, no 49.3 was possible until the nouvelle lecture, and that did not start before mid-December. The dates above come from my background knowledge, apart from the two linked sources for January 2026.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "France uses Article 49.3 on its 2027 state budget before 1 January 2027": **62% Yes** (as of 2026-11-09). This window is two weeks longer than the question's (it runs to 1 January, not 18 December), so the market price likely overstates the chance for this question.
- Kalshi, "France enacts 2027 budget before 1 January 2027": 47%.
- Kalshi, Lecornu announces his departure before 1 December 2026: 7%; before 1 January 2027: 16%.
- I found no Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market that matches this question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 18 November: Senate vote on the PLFSS. A CMP on the PLFSS is expected around the end of November, and the 50-day PLFSS deadline is 26 November.
- 20 November to 8 December: Senate debates the PLF. It votes on 9 December.
- 10 December: possible 70-day ordinance threshold under the count from filing.
- 11 December: deadline to request a separate vote on spending.
- Mid-December: CMP on the PLF. If it fails, the Assembly's nouvelle lecture comes next, which is the first point where a 49.3 is possible. Whether that reading starts before 17 December is the key thing to watch.
- 17 December: possible 70-day ordinance threshold under the count from 9 October. Ordinances are an alternative to 49.3 and would not count for this question.
- 19 December: deadline to file a special finance law. This fallback was used in 2024 and 2025 and implies no 49.3 in December.
- A government collapse at any point, for example a censure over the PLFSS, would rule out a 49.3 on the PLF within the window.

- 2026-10-01: The bill was tabled and the 70-day clock (Article 47) started. Public debate in the Assembly began 2026-10-13. [AN dossier](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/dossiers/PLF_2027)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. 49.3 was not used at first reading, because the Assembly rejected the revenue part and that killed the whole bill.
- The text is now with the Senate. The government can only invoke 49.3 when the bill returns to the Assembly for a new reading after a failed CMP. [LCP](https://lcp.fr/actualites/budget-2027-rejete-quelles-sont-les-prochaines-etapes-au-parlement-444753)
- Key timing:
  - Senate vote on the whole text: 9 December.

  - Nouvelle lecture (the Assembly's new reading): no date set.
  - 70-day deadline: 17 December at midnight. After that, ordinances become possible.
  - So a 49.3 inside the window needs the CMP to fail and the Assembly's new reading to start within about 8 days of 9 December. [NosParlementaires](https://nosparlementaires.fr/actualites/budget-2027-calendrier-assemblee-cinq-semaines)

It does not count here, but it would show the method the government intends to use. - 20 November to 9 December: Senate examines the PLF, with the vote on the whole text on 9 December.
- Before mid-December, no date set: the PLF CMP. If it fails, the Assembly's new reading is the first chance for a 49.3. Whether it is scheduled before 17 December is the main thing to watch.
- 17 December at midnight: the 70-day deadline expires. The government may prefer to let it pass to keep the ordinance option, which would push any action past the window.
- 19 December: deadline to table a special law.
- December: Matignon's compromise meeting, and any non-censure deal with the PS or RN. Any government censure or resignation would also change the picture.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 39 days remain, to 17 December 2026 inclusive (CET). For Yes, the Prime Minister must formally engage the government's responsibility under Article 49.3 on the PLF 2027 in the Assemblée nationale chamber.
